fields: What is the architect's first job during discovery?
Translate ambiguous stakeholder language into testable outcomes, constraints, and requirements.
Why should adjectives such as “fast” or “accurate” be converted into numbers/tests?
So architecture and acceptance can be evaluated objectively.
What ownership questions belong in discovery?
Who approves requirements, owns residual risk, and supports the system in production.
What makes an architecture recommendation useful?
It explains why the chosen option fits the constraints and what trade-offs it accepts.
Why adapt architecture communication by audience?
Different stakeholders need different implications and evidence while the underlying decision remains consistent.
What should accompany a recommendation besides benefits?
Costs, risks, alternatives, reversibility, and supporting evidence.
Why should stakeholders receive measurable expectations for AI systems?
Probabilistic systems cannot responsibly be described with promises of perfect behavior.
What makes a feedback loop actionable?
A signal, trigger/threshold, owner, investigation process, action, and verification.
When should a team re-architect instead of merely iterate?
When a fundamental constraint changed or the architecture pattern itself is the bottleneck.
What should architecture documentation preserve besides diagrams?
Decision context, constraints, alternatives, rationale, assumptions, ownership, and review triggers.
What is the purpose of an ADR?
Record a significant architecture decision and the context/trade-offs behind it.
What lifecycle phases are explicitly in the CCAR-P objective?
Discovery, design, handoff, monitoring, and iteration.
Why cannot monitoring compensate for missing discovery?
You cannot monitor success reliably if requirements and acceptance criteria were never defined.
Functional requirement
What the solution must do.
Non-functional requirement
How the solution must operate, such as latency, availability, scale, residency, or cost.
Trade-off
A deliberate exchange where improving one property costs or constrains another.
Reversibility
How easily and cheaply an architecture decision can be changed later.
Feedback signal
Observed evidence such as user reports, tool errors, cost drift, or safety incidents.
SLA
An agreed service-level expectation/commitment for measurable service behavior.
ADR
Architecture Decision Record documenting a significant decision, context, alternatives, and rationale.
Runbook
Operational guidance for diagnosing, responding to, and recovering from known conditions/incidents.
Handoff
Transition from architecture/design into implementation and operational ownership with acceptance criteria and guidance.
Iteration
Evidence-driven changes after design/launch, accompanied by updated evaluation and documentation.
Discovery should turn vague goals into {{c1::observable acceptance criteria}} before design.
A stakeholder's proposed implementation is not the same as the underlying {{c1::requirement}}.
Unresolved assumptions should have a named {{c1::owner}} rather than remaining implicit.
A strong recommendation explains {{c1::why the option fits the constraints}}, not just what components it uses.
Architecture communication should expose meaningful {{c1::trade-offs}} rather than hiding concessions.
A useful feedback loop has a signal, trigger, owner, action, and {{c1::verification}}.
A user thumbs-down is a {{c1::signal}}, not by itself a complete root-cause evaluation.
An architecture diagram without {{c1::decision rationale}} is incomplete for long-term handoff.
Document decisions that are expensive, risky, or {{c1::hard to reverse}}.
The CCAR-P lifecycle is discovery → design → handoff → monitoring → {{c1::iteration}}.
Handoff is incomplete without explicit {{c1::ownership and acceptance criteria}}.
What requirement category describes what the system must do?
Functional requirement
What requirement category covers latency, availability, scale, and cost?
Non-functional requirement
What term describes the cost/ease of changing an architecture decision later?
Reversibility
What term describes exchanging one architecture benefit for another cost or constraint?
Trade-off
What agreement sets measurable service expectations such as latency or availability?
SLA
What should happen after a feedback-driven change to confirm it worked?
Verification
What document records an architecture decision, context, alternatives, and rationale?
ADR
What lifecycle phase follows design before production operation?
Handoff
A stakeholder says the assistant must be “very fast.” What should the architect ask next?

[{"id":"a","text":"Define a measurable latency target such as an agreed percentile/SLA."},{"id":"b","text":"Choose the fastest model immediately."},{"id":"c","text":"Assume “fast” means under one minute."},{"id":"d","text":"Ignore latency until after launch."}]
a
Discovery converts adjectives into measurable criteria.
A stakeholder asks for an agent but cannot explain the desired outcome. What is the best next step?

[{"id":"a","text":"Clarify the workflow problem, baseline, users, constraints, and success criteria."},{"id":"b","text":"Start implementing an autonomous agent."},{"id":"c","text":"Pick tools before understanding users."},{"id":"d","text":"Treat “agent” as the business requirement."}]
a
Implementation language should not replace requirements discovery.
A proposed workflow handles sensitive data, but nobody has identified who owns residual privacy risk. What is missing?

[{"id":"a","text":"Explicit risk/decision ownership as part of requirements and governance."},{"id":"b","text":"A larger prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"More retrieval documents."},{"id":"d","text":"A second classifier."}]
a
Ownership is a requirement for operating consequential systems.
Two teams disagree on what “correct” means for an extraction task. What should happen before architecture selection?

[{"id":"a","text":"Agree on testable quality criteria and representative examples/evals."},{"id":"b","text":"Choose the strongest model and let it decide."},{"id":"c","text":"Build two unrelated systems."},{"id":"d","text":"Delay defining correctness until production."}]
a
Quality requirements need a shared measurable definition.

[{"id":"a","text":"Revalidate the target against the actual user workflow and business need."},{"id":"b","text":"Treat every inherited SLA as immutable."},{"id":"c","text":"Ignore latency entirely."},{"id":"d","text":"Change the SLA only after deployment."}]
a
Constraints should be justified by the current use case.

[{"id":"a","text":"Connect added autonomy to expected business value, latency/cost impact, and residual risk."},{"id":"b","text":"List every SDK method."},{"id":"c","text":"Show only a component diagram."},{"id":"d","text":"Say agents are the modern choice."}]

[{"id":"a","text":"Identity, trust boundaries, permissions, data flows, and threat controls."},{"id":"b","text":"Marketing slogans."},{"id":"c","text":"Only UI screenshots."},{"id":"d","text":"Only token price."}]

[{"id":"a","text":"A comparison against the agreed constraints and the cost/risk of changing later."},{"id":"b","text":"Only which is newest."},{"id":"c","text":"Only which uses MCP."},{"id":"d","text":"Only which has more components."}]

A stakeholder asks for 100% correctness from a probabilistic support assistant. What is the strongest response?

[{"id":"a","text":"Define measurable quality targets, unacceptable failure classes, escalation, and verification rather than promise perfection."},{"id":"b","text":"Promise 100% if the prompt is long enough."},{"id":"c","text":"Hide error rates."},{"id":"d","text":"Use the strongest model and call it deterministic."}]
a

Users click thumbs-down more often after a release. What should the team do?

[{"id":"a","text":"Treat it as a signal, investigate affected cases/trajectories, identify cause, and verify a targeted fix."},{"id":"b","text":"Assume the model alone is at fault."},{"id":"c","text":"Roll back every time without investigation."},{"id":"d","text":"Ignore it because thumbs-down is subjective."}]
